name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Emergency Cryo-Stasis Pod ECP-1
product_name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Emergency Cryo-Stasis Pod ECP-1
description: A portable cryogenic preservation system that rapidly cools a patient to metabolic stasis temperatures, halting all biological processes including cellular death, hemorrhaging, and toxin propagation. The ECP-1 is designed for pre-hospital care of critically injured or poisoned patients who cannot be stabilized by conventional field treatment — rather than trying to save them on-scene, the patient is preserved in stasis for transport to a definitive care facility. The pod cools the patient to -80°C within 3 minutes using a circulating cryoprotectant that prevents ice crystal formation in tissues, and maintains stasis for up to 48 hours.
story_hooks: A patient was placed in an ECP-1 after a fatal poisoning, preserving them in stasis — but the antidote requires a substance that does not exist in any known pharmacy, and the 48-hour stasis window is ticking.

Someone has been placing living, conscious people in ECP-1 pods as a form of kidnapping — the victims experience 48 hours of frozen awareness before the stasis fails and they wake up in an unknown location.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, utilitarian cryogenic transport pod resembling a reinforced medical stretcher-case hybrid. When closed, it appears as a tapered oval capsule with a glossy upper lid that transitions to a matte undercarriage. The design balances industrial function with emergency-ready aesthetics — every surface suggests rapid deployment and precision medical intervention.
physical_description.dimensions: 185 cm length × 85 cm width × 45 cm height (deployed configuration); collapses to 180 cm × 85 cm × 25 cm for transport
physical_description.weight_description: 25 kg base unit — handheld or two-person carry via integrated grab handles; designed for rapid extraction and loading into emergency transport vehicles
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite shell with internal aluminum cryogenic containment liner; reinforced polymer frame
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal exterior with high-gloss transparent polycarbonate upper lid (frosted internally to diffuse thermal gradients); interior surfaces feature reflective insulation coating with visible frost accumulation during operation
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep gunmetal gray and midnight blue chassis; high-visibility emergency orange trim on latch points and handle accents; crimson Lazarus Pharmaceuticals logo with Φ cost indicator (180,000Φ - 220,000Φ tier pricing) in silver lettering
physical_description.interface_elements: Recessed digital display (8cm tri-color LED readout showing core temperature, stasis duration elapsed, cryoprotectant pressure, and oxygen saturation); physical emergency release lever; membrane keypad (power, initiate stasis, manual override); dual pressure ports (cryoprotectant inlet/outlet marked in blue and red); drainage valve; status indicator lights (steady green = ready, pulsing blue = active stasis, red = emergency)
distinctive_features: Transparent viewing panel with internal condensation patterns revealing frozen atmosphere
Interlocking lid mechanism with redundant mechanical and electronic locks
Cryogenic vapor venting system releasing controlled mist along ventral seams when operating
Integrated power cell indicator strip (5 small LED segments along right edge)
Thermal regulation coils visible through semi-transparent side panels, glowing faintly with operational heat dissipation
Medical-grade quick-disconnect cryoprotectant circulation hoses (coiled and color-coded)
Biolock authentication pad (barely visible fingerprint sensor beneath Lazarus logo)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS embossed in bold sans-serif; serial number laser-etched on interior rim; ISO medical device certification marks on undercarriage; maintenance date stickers; 'CRYOGENIC HAZARD' and multilingual warnings in English/Mandarin/Spanish/Yoruba on all sides; unit type 'ECP-1' in numerals on front panel
physical_description.condition_typical: During operation: visible frost accumulation on upper lid, subtle audible cryo-pump hum, faint vapor wisping from ventral ports. At rest: pristine surface with occasional condensation beading on lid; internal display dark; integrated carrying case clamps visible along sides. Regular field units show minor scuffing on corner guards and handle wear from emergency deployment
